title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023
description: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita 2023 — sourced from bnss.json

children.title: Short title, extent and commencement
children.content:
1. (1) This Act may be called the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
(2) It extends to the whole of India.
(3) This Act replaces the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC).

children.title: Definitions
When police may arrest without warrant
Designated Police Officer
children.content: 37. The State Government shall establish a police control room in every district and at State level, and designate a police officer in every district and at every police station who shall be responsible for displaying information about names and addresses of arrested persons.

children.title: Arrest how made
children.content:
43. (1) In making an arrest the police officer or other person making the same shall actually touch or confine the body of the person to be arrested, unless there be a submission to the custody by word or action.
Provided that where a woman is to be arrested, her submission to custody on an oral intimation of arrest shall be presumed unless circumstances indicate to the contrary.
Provided further that save in exceptional circumstances, no woman shall be arrested after sunset and before sunrise.

children.title: Person arrested to be informed of grounds of arrest and of right to bail
children.content: 47. Every police officer or other person arresting any person without warrant shall forthwith communicate to him full particulars of the offence for which he is arrested or other grounds for such arrest.

parts.title: Information to the Police and Their Powers to Investigate

children.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR, Zero FIR, E-FIR)
children.content: 173. (1) Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing by him or under his direction... Provided that information may be given irrespective of the area where the offence was committed (Zero FIR)... Provided further that e-FIR is permitted provided it is signed within three days by the informant. Preliminary enquiry may be conducted within fourteen days in offences punishable between three to seven years before registering FIR.

children.title: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours (Custody & Remand)
children.content:
187. (1) Whenever any person is arrested and detained in custody, and it appears that the investigation cannot be completed within the period of twenty-four hours... the officer in charge of the police station shall produce the accused before the nearest Magistrate.
(2) The Magistrate may authorize detention in custody (police custody or judicial custody) for a term not exceeding fifteen days in aggregate or in parts during the initial forty days or sixty days out of total sixty or ninety days period.

parts.title: Provisions as to Bail and Bonds

children.title: Bail in bailable offences
children.content: 480. When any person accused of a bailable offence is arrested or detained without warrant by an officer in charge of a police station, or appears or is brought before a Court, and is prepared at any time while in the custody of such officer or at any stage of the proceeding before such Court to give bail, such person shall be released on bail.

children.title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest (Anticipatory Bail)
children.content: 482. (1) Where any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session for a direction under this section that in the event of such arrest, he shall be released on bail.
keywords: Sessions Court and High Court jurisdiction

children.title: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail (Regular Bail)
children.content: 483. A High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person accused of an offence and in custody be released on bail, and if the offence is of the nature specified in sub-section (3) of section 480, may impose any condition which it considers necessary.
keywords: High Court and Sessions Court powers
